name.description: Configuration for name on this Cloud Bigtable resource.
name.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

cluster.description: to as many as possible within 8 cloud regions. Removing the field entirely from the config will cause the provider to default to the backend value. See [structure below](#nested_cluster). -----
cluster.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

project.description: is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This argument can affect security posture or operational safety and should align with organizational policy.

instance_type.description: It is recommended to leave this field unspecified since the distinction between `"DEVELOPMENT"` and `"PRODUCTION"` instances is going away, and all instances will become `"PRODUCTION"` instances. This means that new and existing `"DEVELOPMENT"` instances will be converted to `"PRODUCTION"` instances. It is recommended for users to use `"PRODUCTION"` instances in any case, since a 1-node `"PRODUCTION"` instance is functionally identical to a `"DEVELOPMENT"` instance, but without the accompanying restrictions.
instance_type.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

display_name.description: Configuration for display_name on this Cloud Bigtable resource.
display_name.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

force_destroy.description: Configuration for force_destroy on this Cloud Bigtable resource.
force_destroy.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

deletion_protection.description: When the field is set to true or unset in Terraform state, a `terraform apply` or `terraform destroy` that would delete the instance will fail. When the field is set to false, deleting the instance is allowed.
deletion_protection.rationale: Deletion protection blocks accidental destructive operations on production instances.

labels.description: **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration. Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

terraform_labels.description: The combination of labels configured directly on the resource and default labels configured on the provider.
terraform_labels.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

effective_labels.description: All of labels (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the labels configured through Terraform, other clients and services. ----- The `cluster` block supports the following arguments:
effective_labels.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

cluster_id.description: Configuration for cluster_id on this Cloud Bigtable resource.
cluster_id.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

zone.description: specified, the provider zone is used. Each cluster must have a different zone in the same region. Zones that support Bigtable instances are noted on the [Cloud Bigtable locations page](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/locations).
zone.rationale: Approved-zone enforcement supports data residency and compliance boundaries.

num_nodes.description: If no value is set, Cloud Bigtable automatically allocates nodes based on your data footprint and optimized for 50% storage utilization.
num_nodes.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

min_nodes.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

storage_target.description: !> **Warning**: Only one of `autoscaling_config` or `num_nodes` should be set for a cluster. If both are set, `num_nodes` is ignored. If none is set, autoscaling will be disabled and sized to the current node count.
storage_target.rationale: This argument is primarily operational and should follow platform standards.

kms_key_name.description: Configuration for kms_key_name on this Cloud Bigtable resource.
kms_key_name.rationale: CMEK is required, and key path must match approved project/location/keyring/key constraints.

node_scaling_factor.description: -> **Note**: Removing the field entirely from the config will cause the provider to default to the backend value. !> **Warning:** Modifying the `storage_type`, `zone` or `kms_key_name` of an existing cluster (by `cluster_id`) will cause Terraform to delete/recreate the entire `google_bigtable_instance` resource. If these values are changing, use a new `cluster_id`.
